lead: Paul finishes his farewell at Miletus: keep watch over yourselves and the flock, for which God paid with the blood of his own Son; wolves will come; I commend you to God and to the message of his grace. Then he kneels, prays with them, and they weep. In the Gospel Jesus prays for his disciples: protect them, keep them one, sanctify them in the truth. Psalm 68 calls the kingdoms of the earth to sing to God. The Church also remembers today the Roman martyrs Nereus and Achilleus, and the young martyr Pancras.

set: This is the second half of Paul’s farewell speech to the elders of Ephesus at Miletus, which began in yesterday’s reading. Having looked back on his own ministry, Paul now hands the care of the church over to them, and warns them of dangers to come.
str: v. 28: keep watch over yourselves and the flock bought with God’s own blood.
vv. 29–31: wolves from outside, distorted teaching from within; be alert.
v. 32: I commend you to God and to the message of his grace.
vv. 33–35: Paul’s example: no greed, work with his own hands, help the weak.
vv. 36–38: prayer, tears and farewell at the ship.
kw: The same men are called “elders” in v. 17. The word gives us “bishop”. Their oversight is not lordship but shepherding: “to shepherd the church of God”.
The task Jesus gave Peter, “Tend my sheep” (John 21:16), and that 1 Peter 5:2 gives to the elders. The model is Christ the Good Shepherd.
God “obtained” the Church with blood. The Church is not a human association but a people God has made his own at great cost.
vv: Keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock, of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the church of God that he obtained with the blood of his own Son.

The shepherd must first watch over himself. Textual note: manuscripts differ between “church of God” and “church of the Lord”, and the Greek can be read “with his own blood” or “with the blood of his own one”, that is, his own Son; the NRSV chooses the second and gives the other in a note. Either way, the Church is bought at the price of Christ’s blood.
I know that after I have gone, savage wolves will come in among you, not sparing the flock.
Jesus used the same picture of false prophets in sheep’s clothing (Matthew 7:15). The danger comes from outside and also from within (v. 30).
And now I commend you to God and to the message of his grace,
Paul does not leave them to their own strength. He leaves them to God and to his word, which builds up.
‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’
A saying of Jesus not found in the four Gospels. It shows that sayings of the Lord were remembered and handed on in the early Church beyond what the Gospels record.
ch: The Second Vatican Council teaches that the bishops, by divine institution, have succeeded the apostles as shepherds of the Church, and that they are placed by the Holy Spirit as true shepherds of souls (Lumen Gentium 20; Christus Dominus 2). Paul’s self-portrait, working with his own hands and caring for the weak, remains the measure of every pastor. St Augustine, preaching on shepherds, said that for the people he was a bishop, but with them he was a Christian (in substance).

set: We continue the prayer of Jesus at the Last Supper. Having prayed that the Father may glorify him, he now prays for the disciples he is leaving in the world. They are in the world, but they do not belong to it, and they are being sent into it.
str: v. 11b: Holy Father, protect them, that they may be one.
v. 12: I guarded them; none was lost but the one destined to be lost.
vv. 13–16: my joy in them; the world hates them; protect them from the evil one.
vv. 17–19: sanctify them in the truth; I send them; I sanctify myself for them.
kw: The only time in the Gospels Jesus addresses God in this way. The holy Father is asked to make the disciples holy.

To set apart for God and for his service. In the Old Testament priests and sacrifices were consecrated. Jesus consecrates himself (v. 19) as priest and victim, so that the disciples may be consecrated for their mission.
protect them from the evil one
The same petition as the Lord’s Prayer, “deliver us from evil”, which can also be read “from the evil one”. Jesus does not ask that they be taken out of the world, but kept safe in it.
vv: Holy Father, protect them in your name that you have given me, so that they may be one, as we are one.
The unity of the disciples is modelled on the unity of the Father and the Son. It is a gift to be prayed for, not only a task to be organized.
I am not asking you to take them out of the world, but I ask you to protect them from the evil one.
Christian holiness is not escape. The disciples remain in the world, in families, workplaces and villages, and are kept there by God.
Sanctify them in the truth; your word is truth.
The truth that makes holy is the word of God, and in John the Word is a person (1:1, 14). To be sanctified in the truth is to be made holy by Christ.
And for their sakes I sanctify myself, so that they also may be sanctified in truth.
Jesus consecrates himself as one offers a sacrifice: he gives himself to the Father on the Cross for them. Their holiness flows from his self-offering.
ch: The Church hears this prayer for unity in every work for the unity of Christians. The Second Vatican Council’s decree on ecumenism begins by recalling that Christ prayed that all may be one (Unitatis Redintegratio 2). Pope Benedict XVI, in Jesus of Nazareth, explained that “sanctify” here has a priestly and sacrificial sense: Jesus offers himself, and draws the disciples into his offering (in substance).

qa: What does “the one destined to be lost” mean? Was Judas forced to betray Jesus?

The Greek says “the son of perdition”, a Semitic way of describing one who goes to ruin. It does not mean that God forced Judas. Scripture foresaw the betrayal (Psalm 41:9, quoted in John 13:18), but Judas acted by his own choice. The Church teaches that God’s foreknowledge does not take away human freedom (CCC 600).
rite: Today the Roman calendar offers two optional memorials. Nereus and Achilleus were soldiers in Rome who became Christians and were martyred; the date is uncertain. Pope St Damasus wrote an epitaph for their tomb, saying that they threw down their arms when they believed. Pancras was a youth martyred in Rome, according to tradition at about fourteen years of age, and buried on the Via Aurelia. Like the disciples in today’s Gospel, they lived in the world without belonging to it.
study: Paul tells the elders first to keep watch over themselves. What part of my own life do I need to watch more carefully?
Jesus prays that his disciples may be one. What can I do this week to heal a division in my family, parish or community?
